title: Terraform module for VPC monitoring delivery pipeline
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Goal: Ship a single opinionated Terraform module that deploys the VPC-level monitoring delivery pipeline used by Private (VPC) installations. The module must provision Prometheus (server + remote_write), Grafana (provisioned dashboards + datasource), an OpenTelemetry Collector deployment (receiver/processor/exporter topology), and a configurable log shipping component (Fluent Bit -> object storage or syslog) with safe upgrade and health-check primitives.

Objectives and acceptance criteria:
- One module that is consumable by customers and our private control plane (inputs for network, secrets, instance sizes).
- Idempotent upgrades: module upgrades should not cause alert storms or data loss; we must provide a documented migration path for Prometheus TSDB and Grafana provisioning.
- Health checks & canary: automated canary deploy pattern that validates metrics ingestion, alert evaluation, and log delivery before switching traffic.
- Observability and troubleshooting: module prerenders dashboards and exposes SLO-oriented dashboards to customers by default.
- Secure defaults: TLS for Grafana, OTEL connections over mTLS where supported, KMS integration for any on-disk secrets.
- Terratest acceptance suite that runs against a dev VPC to validate resource creation, smoke queries against Prometheus, Grafana API access, and sample log delivery to S3.

Design constraints and choices:
- Keep provider minimal: module should accept provider aliases (aws, aws.customer) and avoid in-module provider blocks to support multi-account deployments.
- Resource naming: use stable, versioned naming pattern to allow side-by-side canary stacks (eg monitoring-v{module_version}-{env}). Avoid using timestamps in primary names to make state migration testable.
- Prometheus persistence: use EBS with lifecycle hooks for safe snapshot/restore. Document steps for TSDB snapshot and restore during major rollouts.
- Grafana provisioning: use declarative provisioning + dashboard folder structure; don't rely on ephemeral provisioning endpoints that only run on first boot. Store dashboards in module outputs and allow optional Git-backed dashboard sync.
- OTEL Collector: default config implements a split pipeline: receivers (prometheus, otlp), processors (batch, memory_limiter), and exporters (remote_write, otlp->lake). Provide templated config with variables for sampling and rate limits.
- Log shipping: default Fluent Bit DaemonSet with buffering to local disk and periodic S3 flush; support alternate syslog sink for on-prem customers. Provide backpressure knobs and retention settings.

Upgrade strategy:
- Minor upgrades (bugfixes): default rolling update with readiness checks for Prometheus and OTEL; no manual intervention expected.
- Major upgrades (breaking changes): coordination plan: migrate TSDB via snapshot, bring up canary stack, validate terratest suite, cut traffic. Provide terraform-plan gating to fail if nontrivial destructive changes are detected.
- Terraform lifecycle hooks: provide optional null_resource hooks for pre-upgrade snapshot and post-upgrade verification. Include a flag to enable automatic snapshot creation to S3 before any apply that changes storage or statefulset templates.

Health checks and SLO validation:
- Prometheus health: scrape self-metrics, run a set of baseline queries (ingestion-lag, samples-per-second). Module includes a PrometheusRule resource with synthetic alerts suppressed by default.
- Grafana health: provisioning status and API login probe; validate that at least one dashboard is accessible and panels return metrics.
- OTEL Collector health: readiness probe checks exporter connectivity and queue metrics; expose /metrics endpoint for alerts.
- Logshipper health: verify last-successful-upload timestamp and S3 object age; surface failure logs to cluster events.
- Canary workflow: when enabled, module spins up a canary using a different namespace/stack, runs the terratest suite (or CI job), and only migrates route/ingestion after passing thresholds.

Developer & operator notes:
- Testing: provide a dedicated test harness in infra/tests/monitoring_delivery with terratest + github actions that run on PRs affecting module code.
- Docs: Confluence page (link attached) must detail rollback steps, snapshot commands, and emergency cutover steps for data rehydration.
- Cost considerations: include optional flags to disable long-term retention or reduce replica counts for non-production installs.
- Observability of this module itself: export module-level metrics (provision_time_seconds, last_successful_upgrade_timestamp) via a small lambda Terraform resource that reports to Prometheus remote_write.

Out-of-scope for this ticket:
- Deep integration with enterprise SIEMs (this will be a follow-up extension).
- Migration orchestration for >10TB TSDB instances (requires a dedicated migration runbook).

References:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/VPC+Monitoring+Delivery+Pipeline
- Example PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4782
- Acceptance test playbook: infra/tests/monitoring_delivery/README.md
comments: 2025-02-12 — Initial scoping call notes: agreed to keep provider-free module and to expose cloud credentials via provider alias. Aisha to draft variables list.
2025-02-18 — Architecture review: PMs want canary-by-default turned off. Security asked for KMS key rotation docs. Action: add security section and toggles for KMS integration. (Liam)
2025-02-22 — Design feedback from SRE: prefer EBS snapshots before control plane changes; added null_resource pre_snapshot hook prototype. SRE requested a guaranteed snapshot retention of 7 days.
2025-02-27 — PR 4782 opened as a spike implementing OTEL config templating and Grafana provisioning. Uploaded example dashboards and baseline PromQL queries. Link in attachments.

2025-03-03 — Terratest harness: first smoke tests pass in dev account (create/destroy), but Prometheus rule creation failed due to namespace quota; created follow-up ENG-307347 to split namespace provisioning.

2025-03-04 — Next steps: finalize variable naming, add automatic S3 snapshot toggle, schedule security review week of 2025-03-10, and implement canary orchestration in Terraform or by invoking a CI job.
